title: GATE CS Topic Test — Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)
titleEn: GATE CS Topic Test — Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: A 32-bit word 0x12345678 is stored at byte address 0x1000 in a little-endian byte-addressable machine. What byte value is stored at address 0x1000?
questions.explanationEn: In little-endian format, the least significant byte (0x78) is stored at the lowest memory address (0x1000), and the most significant byte (0x12) at the highest (0x1003).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Spatial locality in program execution is exploited by caches primarily through:
optionsEn: Increasing the number of pipeline stages
questions.explanationEn: Fetching a larger cache block brings neighboring memory words into the cache together, directly exploiting spatial locality.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following correctly orders memory types from fastest access time to slowest access time?
optionsEn: CPU Registers < Main Memory (DRAM) < L1 Cache < SSD
SSD < Main Memory (DRAM) < L1 Cache < CPU Registers
CPU Registers < L1 Cache < Main Memory (DRAM) < SSD
L1 Cache < CPU Registers < Main Memory (DRAM) < SSD
questions.explanationEn: Registers are fastest (~sub-nanosecond), followed by SRAM-based L1 cache (~1 ns), DRAM main memory (~50-100 ns), and flash-based SSDs (~tens of microseconds).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Register renaming in modern out-of-order processors is primarily used to eliminate:
questions.explanationEn: Register renaming assigns distinct physical registers to independent writes, eliminating false name dependencies (WAR and WAW) while preserving true RAW dependencies.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: A 2-way set-associative cache uses LRU replacement. For a single set initially empty, the block reference sequence is: A, B, A, C, B, D. How many cache misses occur?
questions.explanationEn: Trace: A(miss:{A}), B(miss:{A,B}), A(hit:{B,A}), C(miss, evict B:{A,C}), B(miss, evict A:{C,B}), D(miss, evict C:{B,D}). Total = 5 misses.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: A byte-addressable computer has a 32 GB main memory. How many bits are required for a physical memory address?
questions.explanationEn: 32 GB = 2^5 × 2^30 bytes = 2^35 bytes. Hence 35 bits are required to address every byte uniquely.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: In horizontal microprogramming, compared to vertical microprogramming:
optionsEn: Only one micro-operation can be executed per clock cycle
Microinstructions are shorter and require more decoding hardware
Microinstructions are wider, allow higher parallelism, and require minimal decoding
Control memory requires fewer bits per word
questions.explanationEn: Horizontal microprogramming allocates dedicated bits to individual control signals, yielding wide microinstructions with minimal decoding overhead and high micro-operation parallelism.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: During the instruction fetch cycle, which register holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched from memory?
questions.explanationEn: The Program Counter (PC) holds the memory address of the next instruction to fetch; the fetched instruction is then loaded into the IR.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: How many 16K × 4 RAM chips are required to build a 128K × 8 memory system?
questions.explanationEn: Number of chips = (128K / 16K) × (8 / 4) = 8 × 2 = 16 chips.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: A 32-bit byte-addressable CPU uses a 32 KB 4-way set-associative cache with 64-byte blocks. How many bits are used for the tag field?
questions.explanationEn: Block offset = log2(64) = 6 bits. Number of lines = 32 KB / 64 B = 512. Number of sets = 512 / 4 = 128, so set index = log2(128) = 7 bits. Tag bits = 32 - 7 - 6 = 19 bits.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn:
A 5-stage pipeline (IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB) has NO operand forwarding; register writes happen in the first half of WB and reads in the second half of ID. Consider:
I1: ADD R1, R2, R3
I2: SUB R4, R1, R5
I3: AND R6, R4, R1
How many total clock cycles are required to execute all 3 instructions?
questions.explanationEn: I1: IF(1) ID(2) EX(3) MEM(4) WB(5). Since I2 reads R1 in ID during WB(5) (write first half, read second half), I2 enters ID in cycle 5: IF(2) stall(3,4) ID(5) EX(6) MEM(7) WB(8). Similarly, I3 needs R4 from I2's WB(8), so I3 enters ID in cycle 8: IF(5) stall(6,7) ID(8) EX(9) MEM(10) WB(11). Total = 11 cycles.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the following RISC instruction sequence running on a 5-stage pipeline (IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB) with full operand forwarding (EX->EX and MEM->EX), where branch outcomes are resolved in ID and no branch prediction is used (not relevant here as there are no branches):
I1: LW R1, 0(R2)
I2: ADD R3, R1, R4
I3: SUB R5, R3, R1
I4: LW R6, 4(R5)
I5: OR R7, R6, R3
How many total clock cycles are required to complete all 5 instructions?
questions.explanationEn: Base cycles for 5 instructions in a 5-stage pipeline = 5 + 5 - 1 = 9 cycles. Load-use hazards: I1(LW R1)->I2(ADD uses R1) adds 1 stall; I2->I3 is forwarded (0 stalls); I3->I4 is forwarded (0 stalls); I4(LW R6)->I5(OR uses R6) adds 1 stall. Total = 9 + 2 = 11 cycles.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: A 64-register file has 2 read ports and 1 write port. Each instruction specifies two source registers and one destination register. How many total bits in an instruction word are dedicated to register specifiers?
questions.explanationEn: 64 registers require log2(64) = 6 bits per specifier. With 3 specifiers (2 source + 1 destination), total bits = 3 × 6 = 18 bits.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: A 64 KB byte-addressable memory is built using 8K × 8 RAM chips. How many address lines are connected directly to each individual RAM chip?
questions.explanationEn: Each chip has 8K = 2^13 locations, so 13 address lines connect to each chip (while the upper 3 address lines feed a 3-to-8 chip-select decoder).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: A 5-stage pipeline (IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB) resolves branch outcomes at the end of the EX stage and uses static 'predict-not-taken'. If 20% of instructions are branches and 60% of branches are taken, what is the effective CPI (assuming no other hazards)?
questions.explanationEn: When a branch is taken, 2 speculatively fetched instructions (in IF and ID while branch is in EX) must be flushed, giving a 2-cycle penalty. Effective CPI = 1 + 0.20 × 0.60 × 2 = 1 + 0.24 = 1.24.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: A disk rotates at 12,000 RPM and has 500 sectors per track, each sector storing 512 bytes. What is the sustained data transfer rate of a track in MB/s (1 MB = 10^6 bytes)?
questions.explanationEn: 12,000 RPM = 200 revolutions/second. Bytes per track = 500 × 512 = 256,000 bytes. Transfer rate = 200 × 256,000 = 51,200,000 B/s = 51.2 MB/s.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: An unpipelined CPU runs at 10 ns per instruction (CPI = 1). A 5-stage pipelined version has a 2.5 ns clock cycle. Due to hazards, 20% of instructions incur 1 stall cycle and 10% incur 2 stall cycles. What is the speedup of the pipelined CPU over the unpipelined CPU?
questions.explanationEn: Pipelined CPI = 1 + 0.20(1) + 0.10(2) = 1.40. Pipelined time per instruction = 1.40 × 2.5 ns = 3.5 ns. Speedup = 10 / 3.5 = 2.857 ≈ 2.86.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about addressing modes are TRUE?
optionsEn: Auto-increment addressing is useful for stepping sequentially through tables or popping from a stack
Indirect addressing requires an extra memory reference compared to direct addressing
Register addressing requires zero main memory accesses to fetch the operand
Immediate addressing can be used as the destination operand of a STORE instruction
questions.explanationEn: Auto-increment simplifies sequential/stack access (A), indirect fetches the pointer from memory first (B), and register operands reside inside the CPU (C). Immediate constants cannot be written to as destinations (D is false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: A synchronous memory bus operates at 400 MHz with a 64-bit data bus width and transfers one 64-bit word per clock cycle. What is its peak data transfer rate in GB/s (1 GB = 10^9 bytes)?
questions.explanationEn: 64 bits = 8 bytes per transfer. Peak bandwidth = 400 × 10^6 transfers/s × 8 bytes = 3.2 × 10^9 B/s = 3.2 GB/s.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: A processor executes 100 memory references: 70% reads and 30% writes. Cache hit rate is 90% for both reads and writes, block size is 32 bytes, and 50% of evicted blocks are dirty. Compare the total main memory traffic (in bytes) of a write-back write-allocate cache vs a write-through no-write-allocate cache (assuming 4-byte writes).
questions.explanationEn: Write-back (write-allocate): 10 misses (7 read + 3 write) each fetch 32 B = 320 B; 50% of 10 evictions are dirty -> 5 × 32 B = 160 B written back. Total = 480 B. Write-through (no-write-allocate): 7 read misses × 32 B = 224 B; all 30 writes go to memory (30 × 4 B = 120 B). Total = 344 B.
